introduction: These readings gather what Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá said of Judaism, of Moses and the prophets of Israel, of the Torah and how it came to be written, and of the Jewish people. They honour the descendants of Abraham and affirm that the truth of the religion of Moses and of Bahá’u’lláh is one. They say that parts of the scriptures are history and not revelation and that its civil laws suited their time, they ask why the Messiah was not recognised, and they promise that the long abasement of Israel will end and its people return to the Holy Land. Many of the passages are notes of talks, some of them severe, and a reader should weigh them as such. The quotations set beside them let Israel’s own tradition speak: Deuteronomy on why it was chosen, Amos on what being chosen costs, the Mishnah and Talmud, Hillel and Maimonides. Paul’s “hath God cast away his people? God forbid”, the Catholic declaration of 1965 and Gandhi’s plea for respect among religions are placed where the readings speak of blame and of destiny.
questions: The readings honour Israel as the people of Abraham and Moses. Deuteronomy says it was chosen because God loved it, and Amos that it would be held the more to account. What does being chosen mean in these sources?

Several readings distinguish what in the Torah is revelation from what is history or later addition. How would a Jew who holds the Torah whole, as the psalmist and the Mishnah do, answer, and what could each learn from the other?
Maimonides taught that the Messiah need work no miracles, and the Talmud warned against calculating his coming. What do these suggest about why a people might not recognise the one it waits for?

Some of these notes speak hard words about the Jews of their time, and one links their sorrow to the crucifixion. How should such passages be read now, in the light of Paul’s “God forbid” and the declaration of 1965?
The readings foretell a return to the Holy Land. What conditions do Leviticus and Exodus attach to holding a land and living among strangers?
Gandhi asked for respect among religions and not one religion. How can a believer hope that others will come to his faith and still honour theirs?

outside.why: Paul, asked what advantage the Jew has, answers: much every way, chiefly that unto them were committed the oracles of God.
The truth that Israel has confessed daily for three thousand years is that the Lord our God is one Lord.
The Qur’an says that the religion ordained for Muhammad is that which was commended to Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus.
Deuteronomy says that Israel was chosen not for its numbers, for it was the fewest of all peoples, but because the Lord loved it.
Isaiah calls on the desolate to sing, for more shall be her children than those of the married wife.
At Sinai Israel is told that if it keeps the covenant it shall be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.

Amos hears God say: you only have I known of all the families of the earth, therefore I will punish you for your iniquities. What does distinction mean in Israel's own scriptures: a privilege, or a heavier account?
Moses told Israel that the nations, hearing its statutes, would say: surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.
The promise to Abraham is that in him all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
Jesus told the Samaritan woman at the well, in so many words, that salvation is of the Jews.

Micah foresees peace in which all peoples walk each in the name of its god, and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God. What harm, to turn the reading's question round, in a people keeping to the faith it has received?
The Qur’an says that God revealed the Torah, wherein is guidance and a light.
Isaiah calls to Zion: arise, shine, for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
Abraham is promised that in his seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed.
Genesis tells how Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, brought bread and wine and blessed Abram.
The Letter to the Hebrews explains his name as King of righteousness, and King of Salem as King of peace.
God says in Numbers that He speaks to a prophet in a dream, but to Moses mouth to mouth.
It was in a cave that Elijah complained: I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life.
The last words of the prophets promise that Elijah will be sent before the great day of the Lord.
Elijah asked the people on Carmel: how long halt ye between two opinions?
The Book of Kings says that a chariot of fire parted them and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. What is gained, and what lost, when such a passage is read as a figure?
Deuteronomy ends with Moses on the mountain, seeing the land he would not enter, and dying there.
Micah asks whether he should give his firstborn for his transgression, and is told what is required instead.
In Exodus Moses says that he is slow of speech and of a slow tongue, and God answers: I will be with thy mouth. How does the scripture's own account differ from the legend of the burnt tongue?
Exodus tells it without excuse: he looked this way and that, slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
Moses was keeping his father-in-law's flock when he saw the bush that burned and was not consumed.
Amos said of himself: I was no prophet, but a herdman and a gatherer of sycomore fruit, and the Lord took me.
Genesis says that Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord, and walked with God.
This is the prayer of Solomon as the Qur’an gives it, asking for a sovereignty such as shall belong to none after him.
The Qur’an tells how Solomon reviewed the birds and asked why he did not see the hoopoe.
Joseph dreamed that the sun, the moon and eleven stars bowed down to him.
God tells Moses to say to Pharaoh: Israel is my son, even my firstborn.
After the wrestling at the ford Jacob is told: thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel.
This is the verse the reading quotes: O Children of Israel, remember My favour wherewith I favoured you.
The Mishnah opens its ethics with a chain of transmission: Moses received the Torah at Sinai and handed it to Joshua, and he to the elders.
The rabbis laid down a principle for such passages: the Torah speaks in the language of men.
Jeremiah already complains that the pen of the scribes has worked falsely.
Spinoza, a Jew of Amsterdam, argued in 1670 that it is as clear as the noonday light that the Pentateuch was not written by Moses, but long after him.
Nehemiah describes Ezra's public reading of the law: they read distinctly, and gave the sense.
Origen asked what intelligent person would suppose that there were evening and morning before there was a sun.
The Torah itself commands: ye shall not add unto the word, neither diminish from it. How would a Jew who holds the Torah whole and from Sinai hear the statement that it is incomplete?
The Talmud holds that a verse never departs from its plain meaning, whatever else is drawn from it. Who decides which parts of a scripture are revelation and which are history?
The psalm says that the law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul. What is at stake for a believing Jew or Christian in dividing the Bible into inspired and uninspired parts?
The Book of Samuel tells David's sin plainly, and has the prophet say to his face: thou art the man. Is a scripture that records the failings of its heroes less trustworthy for it, or more?
Antigone appeals from a king's decree to unwritten laws that no one knows the origin of.
Esther asks the Jews of Shushan to fast for her three days, night and day.
Jesus said that he came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it.
Jesus said: ye have heard an eye for an eye, but I say unto you, resist not evil.
This is the law he was quoting: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.
Jesus gave a rule for reading any law: the sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
Moses records the promise of a prophet like himself, in whose mouth God will put His words.
Moses' blessing says that the Lord came from Sinai, rose up from Seir, and shined forth from mount Paran.
The Letter to the Hebrews argues that by speaking of a new covenant God made the first old.
Maimonides taught that one should not presume the Messiah must work miracles: he is known by what he accomplishes. How does a people decide in advance what will count as the sign?
Luke tells of Simeon, just and devout, who waited for the consolation of Israel and took the child in his arms.
Habakkuk was told: though the vision tarry, wait for it, because it will surely come.
The Talmud curses those who calculate the end, because when the date passes people say he will never come. Is a long expectation a failure of recognition or a discipline of hope?
Ruth the Moabite said to her Israelite mother-in-law: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.
On the road to Emmaus the stranger began at Moses and all the prophets and expounded the things concerning himself.
Stephen asked the council: which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted?
This is the verse of the Qur’an that the reading has in mind.
Isaiah had said it to his own people: behold, the Lord's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save.
The exiles vowed: if I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.
Exodus records the first rebellion: while Moses was on the mountain the people made a molten calf.
The Chronicler gives the same reason for the exile: they mocked the messengers of God, till there was no remedy.
Amos foresaw a famine in the land, not of bread, but of hearing the words of the Lord.

Hillel summed up the Torah for an inquirer standing on one foot: what is hateful to you, do not do to another; the rest is its interpretation; go study. How fairly can a visitor judge the devotion of a people from outside?
The psalm remembers: by the rivers of Babylon we sat down and wept, when we remembered Zion.
Haggai promised those who rebuilt it that the glory of the latter house would be greater than the former.

The Catholic Church declared in 1965 that what happened in the passion cannot be charged against all the Jews then alive, nor against the Jews of today. How should a passage that links a people's sorrow to the crucifixion be read after the history that such a charge helped to bring about?
Lamentations begins: how doth the city sit solitary; she that was a princess is become tributary.
Maimonides himself read Isaiah's wolf and lamb as a metaphor for Israel dwelling in peace with the nations.
Jeremiah speaks of a new covenant, written not on tablets but in the heart.
Jesus said to those who asked for a sign: ye can discern the face of the sky, but can ye not discern the signs of the times?
Zephaniah says that the Lord in the midst of His people will rejoice over them with singing.
Isaiah hears: for a small moment have I forsaken thee, but with great mercies will I gather thee.
Paul says of Israel that the gifts and calling of God are without repentance.
The psalm of return says: the Lord hath done great things for us, whereof we are glad.
Amos ends with the promise that the people will be planted upon their land and no more pulled up.
Leviticus has God say: the land is mine, for ye are strangers and sojourners with me. On what terms, in the Torah itself, is a land held?
Isaiah speaks of a rod out of the stem of Jesse, on whom the spirit of the Lord shall rest.
Jeremiah says: he that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him as a shepherd doth his flock.
The Torah commands: thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger. What does a people that has been unpopular everywhere owe to those among whom it comes to live?
Amos warned those who desired the day of the Lord that it would be darkness and not light for them. Who should be most careful in claiming that the promised day has come?
Isaiah is told: comfort ye, comfort ye my people; speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem.
Isaiah says that the Lord shall gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
Paul asks whether God has cast away His people, and answers: God forbid. Can a people's destiny be spoken of as certain without denying it the freedom to remain what it is?
Gandhi held that what is needed is not one religion but mutual respect among the devotees of different religions. How would a faithful Jew hear the statement that no other course is left?
Deuteronomy promises that the Lord will turn the captivity and gather the people from all the nations.
Zechariah foresees ten men of all languages taking hold of the skirt of a Jew, saying: we have heard that God is with you.
Paul warns Gentile believers that they are branches grafted into an older tree, and that the root bears them. What should later religions remember about the one they grew from?
The psalm asks: pray for the peace of Jerusalem; they shall prosper that love thee.
Isaiah's servant is told that it is too light a thing to restore Israel only: I will give thee for a light to the Gentiles.
This is among the glad tidings of Isaiah: the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.
Isaiah calls on Zion to lift up her voice and say to the cities of Judah: behold your God.
Micah gives the character of the prophets in a line: to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.
The Mishnah teaches that all Israel have a portion in the world to come. What does a tradition that already holds this hope hear in an offer of guidance?
Isaiah heard a voice ask whom shall I send, and answered: here am I; send me.
Some who heard Jesus objected from scripture: shall Christ come out of Galilee? Cometh he not of Bethlehem?

jeremiah-he-that-scattered-israel.text: Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock

zechariah-skirt-of-him-that-is-a-jew.text: Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you

genesis-melchizedek.text: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God. And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all

exodus-slew-the-egyptian.text: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand

exodus-israel-is-my-son.text: And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn

genesis-thy-name-shall-be-israel.text: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed

esther-fast-ye-for-me.text: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish

exodus-eye-for-eye.text: And if any mischief follow, then thou shalt give life for life, Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe

isaiah-hand-is-not-shortened.text: Behold, the Lord's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear

romans-gifts-and-calling.text: As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the father's sakes. For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance

isaiah-light-to-the-gentiles.text: And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth

amos-you-only-have-i-known.text: You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities

genesis-noah-found-grace.text: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord. These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God

deuteronomy-thy-god-will-turn-thy-captiv.text: That then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath scattered thee. If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will the Lord thy God gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee

romans-oracles-of-god.text: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision? Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God

john-salvation-is-of-the-jews.text: Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews

psalm-pray-for-the-peace-of-jerusalem.text: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee. Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces

quran-children-of-israel-remember.text: O Children of Israel! Remember My favour wherewith I favoured you and how I preferred you to (all) creatures.

quran-allahs-hand-is-fettered.text: The Jews say: Allah's hand is fettered. Their hands are fettered and they are accursed for saying so. Nay, but both His hands are spread out wide in bounty. He bestoweth as He will

quran-hoopoe.text: And he sought among the birds and said: How is it that I see not the hoopoe, or is he among the absent?

quran-torah-guidance-and-light.text: Lo! We did reveal the Torah, wherein is guidance and a light

mishnah-all-israel-have-a-share.text: All Israel have a portion in the world to come

exodus-made-them-a-molten-calf.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves: They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed thereunto
